*   The Brightloom checkout API experienced a 43-minute SEV-1 outage on 14 March, causing HTTP 503 errors for 100% of payment-confirmation requests, affecting roughly 18,400 customers and resulting in an estimated 2,150 abandoned orders.
*   The root cause was a configuration error where a merge conflict resolution dropped the `env: staging` guard in a single YAML file, causing a staging-specific reduction of `max_client_conn` from 2000 to 200 to apply to production.
*   The incident was resolved at 09:55 UTC after engineer Sam Okafor identified the incorrect production config value at 09:46, with the error rate returning to baseline by 10:02 UTC.
*   Action items include adding a CI check to reject pooler changes without explicit environment keys (due 28 March), alerting on connection pool saturation above 80% (due 21 March), and refunding an estimated 6,300 EUR in processing fees for affected orders.
*   Positive outcomes included the status page being updated within 6 minutes of the first alert and the configuration rollback taking under 3 minutes.

*   Tidewater CLI 4.2.0, released on 2 October, requires Node 18 or newer and drops support for Node 16.
*   Key features include parallel uploads (up to 8 files, default concurrency 4), resumable transfers via `--resume`, and a new `doctor` command for system checks.
*   Breaking changes involve the removal of the `--legacy-auth` flag (requiring `tidewater login`) and a default switch to JSON output for `tidewater list` when stdout is not a terminal.
*   Fixes address a Windows crash with trailing dots in paths, an incorrect exit code for checksum mismatches, and misleading `--dry-run` help text.
*   Housekeeping updates include moving documentation to docs.example.com, updating the Homebrew formula, basing the Docker image on Alpine 3.19, and acknowledging 14 community contributors.

*   Mobile onboarding completion rose to 61% from 48%, though a 30% drop-off at the notifications permission screen remains; the prompt will move to after the first saved item in Android 3.7.2 and iOS 3.8.
*   The pricing page A/B test showed Variant B (annual-first layout) converting at 4.1% versus 3.4% for the control, leading to a rollout with a 10% holdback for two weeks.
*   The office move is scheduled for 15 January, and the support backlog discussion is deferred to the following Thursday.
*   The design team is hosting a coffee tasting on Thursday.

*   The draft RFC-0042 proposes an optional `Idempotency-Key` header for API v3 to prevent duplicate orders, addressing 312 support tickets (0.4% of orders) caused by client retries.
*   The server stores keys with body hashes and responses in Redis for 24 hours, returning stored responses for matching keys, `422` errors for mismatched bodies, and `409` conflicts for in-flight requests.
*   Storage utilizes the existing Redis cluster with a `idem:` prefix, estimated at under 2 KB per record and 40 GB at peak load, while PostgreSQL was rejected due to write latency.
*   Alternatives such as auto-deriving keys from bodies or making the header mandatory were rejected to avoid merging identical orders and to maintain backwards compatibility, respectively.
*   Open questions remain regarding configurable TTLs per customer and whether to extend coverage to `PATCH` requests, with the author leaning against the latter.

*   The system aims to reduce sprint usage from the current 78% to a target of 30–40% by implementing stamina costs and a "winded" state that limits movement speed and locks sprinting.
*   Stamina mechanics include a maximum of 100 at level 1 (growing by 5 per level to a cap of 150), a drain rate of 12 per second while sprinting, and regeneration of 8 per second after a 1.5-second delay.
*   Sprinting is disabled when carrying heavy objects or in water deeper than knee height, and a full sprint from 100 stamina lasts approximately 8.3 seconds, covering about 62 meters.
*   Interactions with other systems include dodge rolls costing 20 stamina (unaffected by the winded state), cooking buffs adding +20 maximum stamina for 10 minutes, and mounted travel ignoring stamina entirely.
*   Open issues involve art determining if the winded state requires a unique animation (currently reusing the idle-breathing loop) and audio creating a separate heavy-breathing cue (ticket AUD-211).

*   The export failure blocked the customer's month-end reporting due on Friday, but a temporary timeout increase allowed them to successfully complete the export in 27 minutes.
*   The customer’s administrative constraints prevented permission changes until the 10th, and the issue specifically impacted workspaces with approximately 410,000 records.
*   The support team applied a 10 EUR account credit as an apology and committed to keeping the ticket open until the permanent fix releases on 6 Feb.

*   Q3 revenue reached 18.6M USD (up 11% QoQ, 24% YoY), driven by 15.9M USD in subscriptions and 2.7M USD in flat professional services.
*   The company ended the quarter with 1,284 paying accounts (net gain of 73), reduced gross churn to 2.3%, and increased enterprise accounts (over 100k USD ARR) from 41 to 47.
*   Gross margin improved to 74% due to an 8% drop in cloud hosting costs, while operating margin narrowed to -6% from -9% in Q2.
*   Q4 qualified pipeline is 31M USD with a 22% forecast win rate, led by EMEA contributing 38% of new pipeline; headcount grew to 412 employees.
*   Key risks include 2.1M USD in enterprise renewals facing budget freezes in November and potential billing confusion from new pricing tiers launching 1 December.

*   A 21-day pilot study of 96 university students found that daily text-message reminders to wind down 45 minutes before bedtime reduced mean psychomotor vigilance task lapses by 1.8 compared to a control group, while increasing self-reported time in bed by 22 minutes.
*   The study had limitations including a convenience sample of psychology students, a lack of a placebo message for the control group, and a short duration that did not test effects beyond 21 days or during high-stress exam periods.
*   The authors conclude that the reminders may modestly improve morning attention and plan a larger preregistered trial for spring.

*   Effective 1 January, Managed Plus monthly fees increase by 6.5% unless a 24-month renewal is signed before 15 December to lock in current pricing until 30 June.
*   Service levels improve with uptime raised to 99.95% and service credit caps increased from 30% to 50% of the monthly fee.
*   Backup retention extends to 35 days, with an optional add-on available for longer retention at 0.02 EUR per GB per month.
*   Termination notice without cause extends from 60 to 90 days, while phone support shifts to weekdays 07:00-21:00 CET, leaving 24/7 ticket and emergency lines intact.
*   Meridian Backup GmbH is added as a sub-processor for off-site backups, allowing customers 30 days to object in writing.

*   On Day 1, you meet your buddy at 10:00 and your manager at 14:00, and must wait for IT to enable your account before installing work tools.
*   Access to GitHub, the cloud console, and the on-call tool is granted within 48 hours, while production access requires completing a 90-minute security training.
*   During Week 1, you must read the architecture overview, merge a "first PR" by Friday, and attend the Wednesday engineering demo at 16:00.
*   In Week 2, you shadow an on-call shift with your buddy and select a starter ticket labelled `good-first-issue`, with solo pager responsibility starting in week six.
*   Practical details include monthly lunch vouchers, Tuesday kitchen restocking, parking lot closure until month-end, and support via the #new-hires channel or Thursday People team office hours.

*   The level 2 lamp-keeper boss is considered unfair due to a second phase that starts without a visible telegraph, causing three testers to quit.
*   Gamepad players report the jump buffer feels too short, and several testers requested a remappable dash button.
*   The camera clips through walls in narrow corridors, and two testers experienced mild motion sickness during the rooftop chase.
*   Frame rate drops to approximately 40 FPS on a GTX 1050 machine in the market scene, and one unreproduced crash occurred when loading level 3.
*   Two testers found the music loop in level 3 repetitive.

*   The company moves from Levent to Maslak on 30 September, with the old office closing on 27 September at 18:00 and remote work required between 27 and 30 September.
*   The new office opens on 1 October, but only 120 desks are available for the first week, necessitating a rotational work schedule for employees.
*   Personal items must fit into two company-provided kolis by 25 September, while IT handles the transport of monitors and laptops; unlabeled boxes will not be moved.
*   The new location is within walking distance of the metro, offers a company bus departing Levent at 08:15, and provides limited parking for 40 cars with applications due by 18 September.
*   The cafeteria on the 2nd floor will serve only lunch for the first two weeks, and a brief informational meeting regarding potential disruptions is scheduled for 24 September.
